commitResults.messageBody:
Moves all direct System.out printing and Scanner reading out of Chud
into a new Ui class, as the first step of the OOP refactor extracting
Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList out of the main class. Chud's command
handling logic (the switch statement) is unchanged -- only the raw
println/print/Scanner calls were replaced with calls to ui.showX()/
ui.readCommand(), so console output is byte-for-byte identical
(verified via test-ui, 15/15 passing).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList class to wrap the task collection
commitResults.messageBody:
Second step of the Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList refactor. Introduces a
TaskList class wrapping the ArrayList<Task> behind named operations
(add/get/remove/size) and Iterable<Task>, so Chud and Storage work
through a task-list abstraction instead of a raw ArrayList. Storage.load()
still returns an ArrayList<Task> (as in the target design's sample
constructor, `tasks = new TaskList(storage.load())`); Storage.save() now
takes a TaskList.

Because TaskList's method names mirror ArrayList's, Chud's call sites
were untouched apart from the two lines that construct/type the list --
confirming the abstraction is a faithful wrapper, not a behavior change.
Verified via test-ui, 15/15 passing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Parser class to interpret user command text
commitResults.messageBody:
Third step of the Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList refactor. Moves all
"making sense of the raw command line" logic out of Chud's switch
statement into a new Parser class: splitting a line into command word
and arguments, parsing a task index, and parsing each command's
argument shape (a todo's description; a deadline's description and
/by date/time; an event's description and /from/to date/times; an
on query date). Every parsing failure still surfaces as the same
ChudException message as before.

Chud's switch cases now read as "parse via Parser, then execute
against tasks/storage/ui" -- the mutation, persistence, and printing
stay in Chud since that's the orchestration this refactor is building
towards, not something Parser should own. Command.fromCommandWord
dispatch was left where it is (on the Command enum itself), since
it's tightly co-located with the enum's own values.

Verified via test-ui, 15/15 passing -- no message text or console
output changed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Make Storage take its file path from the caller
commitResults.messageBody:
Fourth and final step of the Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList refactor.
Storage no longer hardcodes "data/chud.txt" internally; it now takes
the save file's path via its constructor, with Chud.main passing
"data/chud.txt" -- matching the target design's sample constructor
shape (`new Duke("data/tasks.txt")`).

The path is still resolved through Path.of (which accepts either '/'
or '\' as a separator), so it remains a relative, OS-independent
location; only where the literal path string lives changed, not how
it's parsed.

This also makes Storage reusable/testable against any file path
rather than a single fixed location, which is a natural side benefit
of dependency injection.

Verified via test-ui, 15/15 passing, plus a manual run from a machine
with no pre-existing data folder to confirm first-run creation still
works with the new constructor.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageBody:

description is. Update the unknown-command message and the user
guide to mention find.

cases) and the test-ui console suite (17 cases, including a new one

commitResults.messageTitle: Document key invariants with Java assertions
commitResults.messageBody:
Several methods rely on assumptions that hold by construction but
aren't obvious from a quick read: that parseTaskIndex only ever
returns an in-range index, that TaskList's get/remove are only called
with indices already validated upstream, that Storage.parseTask's
switch always assigns task before it's used, that TaskDateTime always
has a date, and that Command.showTaskAdded is only ever called right
after a task was added.

Add an assert at each of these points stating the assumption, so a
future change that breaks one fails loudly under -ea (Gradle's Test
task already runs with assertions enabled) instead of silently
producing wrong behavior.

Deliberately did not add an assert for Event's from/to ordering:
Parser.parseEventArgs only checks the /from and /to markers' textual
order, not that the parsed dates are chronologically ordered, so that
assumption doesn't actually hold today and asserting it would just
crash on currently-accepted input.

Verified: checkstyleMain/checkstyleTest and the full JUnit suite pass
under assertions, and a manual `java -ea` console run exercises every
new assert (add/mark/list/delete, plus loading from the save file)
without tripping any.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract shared add-task sequence out of the three add-commands
commitResults.messageBody:
AddTodoCommand, AddDeadlineCommand, and AddEventCommand each ended
with the identical three-line sequence: add the new task to the list,
save the list to disk, then re-fetch the task that was just inserted
(via tasks.get(tasks.size() - 1)) just to hand it to showTaskAdded.
The only thing that varied between the three commands was which Task
subtype got constructed -- everything after that was copy-pasted.

Per the course's code quality guidelines (DRY: don't repeat the same
logic in multiple places), replace Command's showTaskAdded helper
with a single addTask(tasks, ui, storage, task) that does the add,
save, and confirmation-print together, using the task reference the
caller already has instead of looking it back up. Each add-command
now reduces to constructing its Task and calling addTask(...) once.

This also removes a small latent bug risk: fetching the task back out
of the list by position only happens to be correct because nothing
else can insert between the add and the fetch; passing the reference
directly removes that assumption entirely.

Verified: checkstyleMain/checkstyleTest, the full JUnit suite, and the
console test-ui suite (17/17) all pass unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams to filter tasks in FindCommand and OnCommand (#3)
commitResults.messageBody:
FindCommand and OnCommand both manually looped over every task with
a hand-rolled counter, incrementing and printing only when a
condition held (matchesKeyword / occursOn). The filtering condition
was buried inside an if-statement rather than expressed as what it
actually is: a predicate over the task list.

Add TaskList.stream(), exposing a Stream<Task> over the underlying
list alongside the existing Iterable support. Rewrite both commands
to select matches with tasks.stream().filter(...).collect(...), then
print the resulting (already-filtered) list with a plain indexed
loop. Streams are used only for the selection step, which is a
natural fit for a declarative filter; the numbering/printing step
stays an ordinary loop, since 1-based sequential numbering is
inherently positional and doesn't gain anything from being forced
into the stream pipeline.

Verified: checkstyleMain/checkstyleTest, the full JUnit suite, and the
console test-ui suite (17/17) all pass unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add list /sort <key> [asc|desc] to sort the task list (#4)
commitResults.messageBody:
There was no way to reorder tasks -- they always stayed in whatever
order they were added. Add an optional /sort argument to list that
permanently reorders the task list (and re-saves it), so subsequent
mark/unmark/delete task numbers reflect the new order.

Add getDescription()/isDone()/getSortDate() accessors to Task, with
getSortDate() overridden in Deadline (its /by date) and Event (its
/from start date) -- mirroring the existing occursOn(LocalDate)
override pattern already used for the `on` command. Add SortKey
(date/description/type/done, each owning its own Comparator<Task>)
and SortDirection (asc/desc) enums, and TaskList.sort(Comparator),
which relies on ArrayList.sort's existing stability to keep tied
tasks in their original relative order for free.

A todo has no date and always sorts last under the date key in both
directions -- achieved by wrapping only the non-null date ordering in
reverseOrder() rather than reversing the whole nullsLast comparator,
which would otherwise flip Todos to the front on desc.

Parser.parseListSortArgs validates the /sort marker, key, and
optional direction, returning null for a plain `list` (unchanged
behavior) or throwing a specific ChudException otherwise. No new
command word was needed, and the GUI needed no changes at all --
MainWindow already routes every typed line through Parser.parse +
Command.execute unchanged.

Added JUnit coverage for the new accessors, enums, and TaskList.sort,
plus a new "Sort the task list" console test-ui case (recorded via
the test-ui skill's --record mode) covering every key/direction
combination and the four validation-error paths. Documented the new
option in README.md.

Verified: checkstyleMain/checkstyleTest, the full JUnit suite, the
console test-ui suite (18/18), a GUI smoke run, and a manual console
session confirming mark/delete act on the new sorted numbering and
that the reordered list is what's actually written to chud.txt.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Chud's avatar and asymmetric, error-aware dialog boxes
commitResults.messageBody:
The user's typed input and Chud's replies looked like two sides of
the same chat bubble, but this is a person entering commands at an
app, not two people messaging each other -- and errors looked
identical to normal replies, easy to miss in a long reply.

Give the two sides different visual weight: the user's line becomes a
smaller, monospaced, avatar-free echo of what was typed, while
Chud's reply keeps its avatar, more padding, and a wider bubble,
since replies like `list`/`find` can run several lines. Style an
error reply distinctly (its own CSS class, wired up via a new
GuiUi.hasError()) so a bad command stands out instead of blending in.

DialogBox now binds each bubble's max width to a fraction of the
dialog column's width (via the new containerWidth parameter) instead
of a fixed pixel value, so bubbles resize sensibly with the window.

Verified: checkstyleMain/checkstyleTest, compileJava, the full JUnit
suite, the console test-ui suite (18/18, unaffected since none of
this touches the console Ui), and a GUI smoke run confirm the avatar
loads and the app launches without errors.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make the input bar responsive instead of fixed-pixel anchors
commitResults.messageBody:
The text field and Send button were positioned with manually-tuned
pixel offsets (rightAnchor=88 on the field to leave room for a
right-anchored button), which is brittle and doesn't reflow cleanly
on resize.

Wrap both controls in an HBox with the text field set to
HBox.hgrow="ALWAYS": the field now grows to fill available width and
the button keeps its natural size, with no magic numbers to keep in
sync. Also bump the default window size (400x500 -> 420x600) since
task-list replies read more comfortably with a bit more room.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix NullPointerException risk in Storage.save with no parent dir
commitResults.messageBody:
Path.getParent() returns null for a path with no directory component
(e.g. "chud.txt" instead of "data/chud.txt"), and
Files.createDirectories(null) throws NullPointerException rather
than an IOException -- so it would have bypassed save()'s existing
IOException handling entirely and crashed the whole program instead
of degrading gracefully. Unreachable today (the save path is always
the hardcoded "data/chud.txt"), but a latent trap for any future
change to how that path is built.

Only call createDirectories when there's an actual parent to create.

Verified: checkstyleMain/checkstyleTest and the full JUnit suite pass,
including a new test confirming save() works with a no-parent path.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a graceful fallback for unexpected command errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Every command's expected failure mode is ChudException, caught and
shown to the user as a normal error message -- but an unanticipated
bug in a command's own logic (a RuntimeException) had no safety net
in either the console loop or the GUI: it would have propagated out
and crashed the whole session instead of just failing that one
command.

Add a catch (RuntimeException e) fallback after catch (ChudException
e) in both Chud.main's loop and MainWindow.handleUserInput, showing
a generic "something broke (ExceptionType). Try again." message
instead of crashing. In the GUI, also move Parser.parse(input) inside
the try block (it was outside it, unlike the console version) so a
future change to parsing is covered by the same safety net, and guard
the later command.isExit() check against command staying null if
parsing/execution never produces one.

Also make DialogBox's avatar image loading defensive: a missing or
corrupt chud.png resource now falls back to no avatar (skipped
entirely) instead of throwing at class-load time and taking down the
whole GUI over a cosmetic asset.

Verified: checkstyleMain/checkstyleTest, the full JUnit suite, the
console test-ui suite (18/18, unaffected -- none of these paths are
reachable through normal input), and a GUI smoke run all pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'A-ErrorHandling'
commitResults.messageBody:
Hardens error handling: fixes a NullPointerException risk in
Storage.save for a parent-less path, adds a RuntimeException safety
net around command execution (console and GUI) so an unexpected bug
can't crash the whole session, and makes the GUI's avatar loading
degrade gracefully if the image asset is missing or corrupt.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rewrite the User Guide and consolidate it into docs/
commitResults.messageBody:
docs/README.md was a stale User Guide predating the GUI, the sigma-
grindset personality voice, the list /sort feature, and the recent
error-handling hardening -- every example in it showed the old plain
phrasing ("Got it. I've added this task:", "OOPS!!!", etc.) and it
never mentioned sorting at all. Meanwhile the root README.md had all
the current, accurate command info, but was framed as a developer/

Consolidate into a single, up-to-date User Guide at docs/README.md:
a Quick Start (Java 25, get/build the jar, run it), the actual GUI
screenshot, every command with its exact current-voice example output
-- each one verified by actually running the command, not
hand-typed from memory -- the list /sort feature, and a note on how a
missing or corrupted save file degrades gracefully instead of
crashing. Drop the developer-setup content that doesn't belong in a
user-facing guide, and remove the now-redundant root README.md.

Verified: checkstyleMain/checkstyleTest, the full JUnit suite, and
the console test-ui suite (18/18) all pass unaffected, since this is
a docs-only change.
